summary: Sudden elevation in 5xx rate: API gateway 502/503 flood correlated with upstream runtime crashwave during large embedding/stream mix
description: Customer ClipperAI reports a sharp increase in 5xx responses starting ~2026-03-13T21:12:00Z. API gateway metrics show a sudden rise in 502/503 errors and streaming disconnects. Support observed repeated upstream runtime crashes and fast restarts on a subset of ephemeral runtimes handling mixed embedding + streaming workloads for the customer. Initial mitigation: traffic was re-routed to fallback region and a temporary rate-limiter was enabled on the tenant. Impact: degraded generation and embedding throughput for multiple endpoints (chat and bulk embeddings) for ~28 minutes for the customer and some co-tenants on shared host pools.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer submitted concurrent long-running streaming sessions (chat) while also uploading a large embedding bulk job (~60k items) using multipart upload.
2) Client retried aggressively after early 50x responses.
3) Combined traffic produced connection churn at the API gateway, causing increased backend hedged retries and prefetch contention.
4) Observe API gateway 5xx rate and upstream runtime restarts in metrics dashboards.
observed_metrics:
- api-gateway 502/503 rate increased from baseline 0.2% to 18% between 21:12-21:40 UTC.
- mean latency for first byte (chat) rose from 120ms to 1.8s.
- ephemeral runtime restart count spiked: +76 restarts across 18 hosts in the runpool.
- nvml/gpu driver errors found on 7 hosts (driver timeouts) around first crash wave.
- scheduler queue length (prefetch) increased by 4200 items during peak.

[2026-03-13T21:13:02Z] api-gw-54 WARN upstream-502: connection-reset-by-peer tenant=clipperai request_id=abc123

[2026-03-13T21:16:41Z] scheduler ERROR backpressure: accept-queue-depth=8192 target=2048
investigation_notes:
- Correlation points to a tenant-level burst: mixing large embedding upload with many long-lived streaming sessions caused backlog in accept/priority queues.
- Prefetch/kv-cache layer hit lock contention (kv-lock) and slow IO on a subset of nvme backs. That produced blocking in serving-runtime threads which caused watchdog timeouts and runtime restarts.
- Runtime restarts triggered upstream connection resets seen at api-gateway which reported 502/503.
- Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity because the backpressure was queue-based (accept-queue growth) rather than CPU-only.
- GPUs on affected hosts showed elevated iowait and sporadic NVML timeouts consistent with heavy embedding IO + model loading churn.
- No evidence of model-code bug in stack traces; stack traces show worker thread blocked in kv read path and then watchdog kill.
comments: Support (Aisha): 2026-03-13T21:20Z - Confirmed spike on dashboards and customer impact. Enabled tenant rate-limit at 30 RPS and paused background prefetch for the tenant as an emergency mitigation.
SRE (Diego): 2026-03-13T21:26Z - Identified 7 hosts with NVML timeouts. Drained affected runpool nodes and initiated rolling restart to clear GPU driver state for those hosts.
Customer (ClipperAI - K. Patel): 2026-03-13T21:30Z - Reported large embedding job was started as a catch-up; asked for guidance on safe concurrency limits.

Eng (Lina Xu): 2026-03-13T21:45Z - Noted accept-queue growth correlated with concurrent streaming keep-alive churn and multipart embedding upload split across many small chunks. Recommends upload coalescing and backpressure on client SDK.
Support (Aisha): 2026-03-13T22:05Z - Traffic re-routed to fallback route for critical customer flows; error rate returned to baseline ~21:40 UTC. Customer confirmed partial recovery.
SRE (Diego): 2026-03-13T22:20Z - Completed node restarts; no further NVML timeouts seen. Post-mortem started and follow-ups assigned.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: tenant rate-limits and prefetch pause prevented further immediate crashwaves. Affected nodes were drained and restarted to clear NVML timeouts. Customer was advised on concurrency limits and upload patterns. Full resolution requires follow-up infrastructure hardening and SDK guidance to avoid similar bursts.
resolution_notes:
- Temporary actions: tenant rate-limit (30 RPS) until client adjusts; paused tenant prefetch; drained and restarted 8 affected nodes.
- Permanent actions planned (see follow_up_actions).
- No lasting data loss; telemetry and logs preserved for postmortem.
follow_up_actions: Postmortem write-up to include timeline, root cause, and mitigation playbook (owner: Diego) - due 2026-03-17
Implement tenant-level burst detector that can apply adaptive backpressure instead of global hedged-retries (owner: Lina) - RFC by 2026-03-24
Add prefetch circuit-breaker to avoid kv-lock cascade under heavy embedding uploads (owner: Runtime team) - patch PR #9901
Customer SDK update: recommend coalesced embedding upload and client-side concurrency limiter; add guidance to docs (owner: DevEx) - doc PR by 2026-03-20
Improve runpool health checks to detect NVML soft-failures earlier and proactively drain nodes (owner: SRE) - ops ticket INT-2029
